chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about tayammum. So he struck the ground with his two palms, then wiped his face with them. Then he struck the ground with his left hand and wiped with it from his elbow to the fingertips, once over its back and once over its palm. Then he struck the ground with his right hand, then did with his left as he had done with his right. Then he said: This is tayammum in place of that in which ghusl is required, and in wudu (ablution): the face and the two hands up to the elbows; and he omitted that over which wiping of the head and the two feet had been required, so one does not perform tayammum with earth for that.

As for what this hadith includes, namely that he wiped from the elbow to the fingertips, once over its palm and once over its back, it is to be understood according to what we have previously mentioned regarding taqiyyah or the ruling, in accordance with what has passed in the interpretation of the report of Sama'ah. And what it includes of separating the strike of the right and the left in wiping the two hands does not require that the strikes be three, because what is considered in each one of the two strikes is that it be with both hands together; so if, in one of the two strikes, the two hands are separated, that is not contrary to that.

As for the report of Dawud ibn al-Nu'man from Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام, containing the story of 'Ammar, it does not require that, in ghusl from janabah, one strike be deemed sufficient, since what is stated in it is that he placed his two hands upon the ground, then raised them and wiped with them his face and his hands slightly above the wrists. For it only reports the manner of performing the act in tayammum, and it does not say that he did that with one strike or two strikes. Since that possibility exists, we interpret the report according to what has come in the detailed reports that we have cited.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity invoked in reconciling the report
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed with earth or clean ground in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl
key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: earth or clean ground used for tayammum
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath requiring a substitute form of purification when water cannot be used
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: ritual ablution whose substitute in tayammum involves wiping the face and hands
key_terms.مِرْفَقَهُ: the elbow, marking the upper limit of the wiping described in the report

ai.seo_question: How many strikes are required in tayammum according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report discusses the method and number of strikes in tayammum, including how the face and hands are wiped. It also explains how apparently differing reports are reconciled by referring to more detailed narrations and established legal interpretation. The passage is significant in Shia fiqh for clarifying procedural details of tayammum in relation to wudu (ablution) and ghusl.
